messages:
marta: Heads-up — we're seeing a correlated spike in apiserver 5xxs in us-west-2. Graphs show etcd WAL iops jump coinciding with a GPU autoscaler burst after yesterday's model rollout. controller-manager leader flipped twice. :rotating_light:
jun: Oof. Any immediate mitigation? can we pause the autoscaler or drain the new GPU nodes?
vikram: I already throttled the autoscaler policy at 12:37 UTC, but there was a ~4m window where ~120 GPU pods started attaching and hitting persistent volumes. Volume iops peaked.
hayden: Logs show kvstore fsyncs piling up. attaching logs: ```ts=2026-03-10T12:35:01Z etcd wal: fsync delayed=120ms write=3ms``` looks like IO saturation on WAL devices.
lin: Are these customers on bursty batch jobs or continuous inference? might be large-batch warmups from the rollout.
marta: Looks like a single canary rollout triggered distributed preloading on model shards — bursts across many hosts. We didn't throttle prefetch.
jun: For immediate relief: 1) pause rollout 2) scale down GPU attach concurrency by setting default maxSurge/parallelism for rollout controller 3) bump etcd WAL compress throttles?\haysden: (typo) hayden: I mean bump etcd compaction cadence or tune writeback? compaction won't help WAL iops immediately. We should reduce attach concurrency and apply IO QoS on WAL devices — create a cgroup or throttle at host level.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2314 — etch-wal-iops-gpu-burst (severity=high)
vikram: Quick temporary fix: add a taint to new GPU nodes and cordon so no more auto-attaches, then sequentially untaint when IO stabilizes. I'm adding a script to cordon by label: ```kubectl label nodes gpu-new cordon=true``` (planned run in 2m)
lin: Good. Also consider switching heavy hitters to warm-cache instances with local ephemeral storage to avoid PV fsyncs. That requires orchestrating a model cache config in the runtime.
marta: Agreed. Ops plan: pause canary, cordon new GPU hosts, scale down attaching pods to 10% concurrency, flip controller-manager to standby leader mode if leadership churn continues.
jun: Controller logs when leader flipped: ```controller-manager: WARNING: leader changed from controller-1 to controller-3 (lease lost after 18s)``` suggests lease renewals delayed due to API errors. If apiserver is overloaded by watch fanout, leader renewals fail.
hayden: We should temporarily increase lease duration and renewDeadline on controller-manager to avoid flapping while we stabilize IO. But that's intrusive. Alternative: route some read-only traffic away from control plane by setting routing policy to regional fallback.
vikram: Cost question: if we artificially smooth GPU autoscaler bursts (reserve capacity or gradual ramp) we'll pay for idle GPUs. What's the monthly delta if we reserve a small buffer in us-west-2?
lin: Back-of-envelope: reserving 20 GPUs at on-demand vs reserved discounts — committed reserved reduces unit cost ~30%. If we reserve minimal capacity for hotspots we can reduce incident risk and net cost if utilization stays >40%. Need finance input.
marta: For this incident, priority is stability not cost. Postmortem action item: add autoscaler burst limits, make prefetch opt-in for model rollouts, and add WAL iops alerting per-host.
jun: Also add a controller-manager alert for leader-flip-count > 1 within 5m and tie to automatic rollback of in-flight rollouts.
ops-bot: Note: adding action items to INC-2026-2314 ticket.
vikram: After we cordon and reduce concurrency, WAL iops down to baseline within 6m. apiserver 5xx rate back to normal. Monitoring shows small residual leader lease jitter but no further flips.
lin: Follow-ups: - run a simulated scale test with prefetch enabled in staging (use synthetic attach load) - add IO throttling recipe for hosts mounting PVs used by model caches - explore reserving a 10% GPU buffer in high-traffic regions
marta: I'll write the postmortem draft later today. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
jun: Great work. Let's keep this ticket open until postmortem and quota/autoscaler config changes land.
hayden: I'll open a PR for controller-manager lease tuning with a canary flag so we can test shorter risk window.
vikram: Uncordoning nodes gradually now. will update when last node uncordoned.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-2314 updated: status=stabilized, responders=[marta,jun,vikram,hayden,lin]
